LA VERNE YOUTH & FAMILY ACTION COMMITTEE
  Minutes of the Regular Meeting
  October 22,2019
1. A regular meeting of the Youth & Family Action Committee was called to order by
  Mayor Don Kendrick at 6:30 p.m.

2. Executive Board Members present
  Executive Board
  Don Kendrick, Chair
  Robin Carder, Council Member
  Matthew Lyons, BUSD
  Carolyn Cockrell, BUSD
  Denise Fisher, Resident

  Mark Rodgers, BUSD
  Eric Podley, BUSD
  Jason Lorge, Resident
  Ron Serven, Resident
  Vanessa Hess, Resident
  Patty Hess, Resident
  Doug Strange, Resident
  Krista Chakmak, Resident
  Lacy Flippin, FairPlex
  Sam Gonzalez, LVPD
  Hollie Savage, LVPD
  Francisco Cambero, LVPD
  David Yim, Tri-City
  JR Ranells, City of La Verne

3. Review of Minutes  Minutes for the September 24th meeting were
  approved.

4. POA Presentation  La Verne Police Officers' Association (POA)
  President Mark Gutierrez provided the group an
  update on the POA's first golf tournament noting that
  it was very successful. The POA had reviewed
  several potential options to donate the proceeds of
  the golf tournament to and selected YFAC because
  of its community contributions. Mark presented a
  check to Mayor Kendrick for $4,000 to be used for
  YFAC programs.

5. Tax Measure lnfo  Mayor Kendrick introduced City Manager Bob Russi
  to the group. Bob provided a presentation on the
  proposed tax measure that would be placed on the
  March 2020 ballot for resident consideration.
 Youth & Family Action Committee Minutes October 22,2019, page2

  Members of the group asked questions and provided
  prospective on the proposed measure.

6. School Resource Officer  School Resource Officer (SRO) Frankie Cambero
  provided information on the recent potential threats
  against Bonita High School. Frankie noted that the
  Bonita Unified School District handled the situation
  exceptionally well. Frankie also reported that vaping
  continues to be a problem amongst the community's
  youth and that it is not just affecting the "usual
  suspects." Even kids that would traditionally be
  considered immune from getting into trouble have
  been involved with vaping. The group discussed
  efforts by Congress and the state legislature to
  restrict vaping products and what additional efforts
  could be taken. Jessica Vozella with the American
  Lung Association will be providing a presentation at
  an upcoming YFAC meeting.

7. BUSD Report  Mark Rodgers with the BUSD provided a report on
  activities within the district. Mark noted recent K-9
  visits to schools as well as personnel training on
  detection of students under the influence. Mark also
  updated the group regarding the additional mental
  health resources on school campuses.

8. Public Safety Open House  Community Services Officer Hollie Savage provided
  the group information on the upcoming Public Safety
  Open House. Hollie also presented the group with
  information on proposed safety signs to be distributed
  at the City's booth on behalf of YFAC during the open
  house. The board approved purchasing the signs for
  $425.

9. Teen Summit  Bill Aguirre with the City of La Verne provided an
  overview of the upcoming Teen Summit. Bill also
  invited YFAC members to stop by the event if they
  were interested.

10. Regular Tips  JR Ranells with the City of La Verne provided
  information on potential priorities for the group to
  consider regarding doing regular tips to the community
  that would be put on various social media platforms
  The group directed staff to focus on regular tips rather
  than regular videos produced by Proud Digital Media
  and that internal staff be the ones creating the content.
 Youth & Family Action Committee Minutes October 22, 2019, page 3

1'1 . Round Table  Jessica Vozella shared information on recent studies
  on vaping and its harmful effects as well as information
  on how to get help.

  BUSD Board Member Matt Lyons thanked the Police
  Department as a parent and board member for their
  response to the recent threat. Matt also mentioned the
  Grace Miller Fall Festival and the Police Department's
  Pink Patch Project.

  Lacy Flippin with Fairplex shared information on
  resources and offerings from her organization.

  Vanessa Hess inquired about the new high school
  representative. Mr. Podley noted they are working on
  getting the new person on board and expect it to be
  done soon.

  Ron Serven thanked the City for the presentation on
  the tax measure and noted he is looking forward to
  working with partners on solving problems in the
  comm unity.

  Jason Lorge shared his appreciation for YFAC
  supporting the safety sign distribution at the Public
  Safety Open House.

  JR noted his son's gratitude and excitement after
  visiting Heritage Park's Pumpkin Patch and how lucky
  our youth are to be in La Verne.

  Council Member Robin Carder thanked the group for
  their participation and discussion. Robin also
  introduced Doug Strange and noted his connection to
  the Active Transportation Committee.

  Patty Hess shared information on Claremont's efforts
  to initiate a teen group on suicide loss as well as other
  information related to suicide prevention.

 12. Public Comment  Michael Gaydos noted the recent losses suffered at
  Bonita High School has been difficult but has brought
  people together.

 '1
  3. Next Meeting  The next YFAC meeting is scheduled for November
  26,2019 at 6:30 P.m.

 14. Adjournment  The meeting was adjourned at 8:25 p.m.
